title: Finite ideal generator bound from localized conormal generators
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq P$ a finitely generated ideal, $q\in\operatorname{Spec}(P/I)$, $Q$ its inverse image in $P$, and $c\in\mathbb N$. Write $A=P_Q$ and $B=(P/I)_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The conormal module is the $(P/I)$-module $I/I^2$, and let $N=(I/I^2)_q$ be its module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. If a family $g:\{0,\ldots,c-1\}\to N$ spans $N$ over $B$, then the least number of generators of the ideal $IA\subseteq A$ is at most $c$. In Lean this number is the spanFinrank of the ideal $I$ mapped to $A$.

proof.text: Represent each g_i by z_i/s_i in the localization of I/I² at q. Lift z_i to f_i in I. Let J be the ideal generated by the f_i and N0 their conormal span over P/I. Each g_i lies in the localization of N0 because its denominator s_i is outside q. Since the g_i span, that localized submodule is the whole localized conormal module. These are precisely the fraction and equality formulas of module localization.

The conormal span N0 consists of classes of elements of J: check the assertion on generators and preserve it under addition and scalar multiplication, lifting each quotient-ring scalar to P. For z in I, membership of its localized class in the localization of N0 supplies w in N0 and a denominator s with s[z]=w after localization. The localization equality criterion supplies s′ outside q for which s′s[z] belongs to N0 before localization. Lift s′s to t in P outside Q and represent this class by a in J. Then tz-a belongs to I², so tz belongs to J+I².

Map tz in J+I² to A. Since t lies outside Q its image in A is a unit. Cancellation proves IA is contained in JA+(IA)². The ideal IA is finite and lies in the maximal ideal of A because I is contained in Q. Nakayama, with module IA and submodule JA, yields IA contained in JA; the opposite containment follows from J contained in I.

The images of the c elements f_i span JA=IA. The cardinality of their range is at most c, so the minimum size of a generating set is at most c. This also proves the empty-family case, where IA is zero.

theorem spanFinrank_localized_ideal_le_of_conormal_generators
    {P : Type u} [CommRing P] (I : Ideal P) (hI : I.FG)
    (q : PrimeSpectrum (P ⧸ I)) (c : ℕ)
    (g : Fin c → LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl I.Cotangent)
    (hspan : Submodule.span (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) (Set.range g) = ⊤) :
    (I.map (algebraMap P
      (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))).spanFinrank ≤ c
